stem: Which layers do most product teams build in?
explanation: Buy the model, rent the hardware, build on top.

stem: Self-hosting an open model means taking ownership of…
options: Serving and hardware too — GPUs, capacity, an inference server, upgrades, on-call
explanation: It can be right for privacy or unit economics; it is an operations commitment.

options: You can run the model — not that data/recipe are open or that the licence allows your use

stem: Which is NOT one of the four model kinds in this lesson?
explanation: Small/specialised is the fourth; expert systems are outer-ring AI, not models you pick here.

stem: Customer text must stay in-region. Which options survive?
options: Self-hosting, or a hosted model via a cloud platform with in-region processing and a suitable agreement
explanation: Region and data handling are serving-layer properties; check the contract.

stem: How does the hardware layer reach a product engineer?
options: Per-token pricing, latency that scales with tokens, rate limits

stem: A vendor ships a new model version. Which layer changed and what should you do?
options: Training & data — run your evals before adopting; pin versions
explanation: Behaviour shifts with training; evals notice.

options: Hosted first, gateway in front so it is reversible, self-host by exception
explanation: Keeps the choice reversible while learning what the workload needs.

options: Alongside a generation model, for search/RAG/clustering

stem: When does a small/specialised model beat a frontier one?
options: Classification, extraction, routing where latency and cost matter and it can be fine-tuned
explanation: Settle with an eval on real data.
